scope: All 422 event records scanned for temporal classification, inclusive endpoints, adjacent-year leakage, ongoing cutoff semantics and linkage to the existing source-review ledger. Recent space milestones, ongoing Ukraine conflict and emergency/pandemic distinctions rechecked against primary sources. This does not independently reverify all historical facts in the older ledger.
policy: Human milestones use their recorded year only. Intervals use inclusive documented years; ongoing 2026 endpoints are coverage limits. Approximate point dates remain approximate, without invented uncertainty intervals. Fossils retain their explicitly disclosed million-year age window.

events.title: Vietnam War aftermath: Vietnamese refugee departures
events.sourceReview: UNHCR’s Flight from Indochina describes the exodus beginning in 1975; its regional update records the CPA’s formal conclusion on 30 June 1996.

events.title: Soviet–Afghan War: refugees in Pakistan and Iran
events.sourceReview: The UN mission’s UNHCR history links large-scale flight to the Soviet occupation beginning in 1979. The window isolates the war phase and explicitly leaves subsequent displacement open.

events.title: Bosnian War: refugees and internal displacement
events.sourceReview: USHMM dates the Bosnian War to 1992–1995 and documents displacement. Bosnia’s migration research records Croatia and Germany among host countries.

events.title: Rwandan genocide and war: regional refugee crisis
events.sourceReview: UNHCR describes the mid-1990s exodus into Tanzania and Zaire and large-scale returns in 1996; the selected interval is not the whole history of Rwandan exile.

events.title: Syrian war: refugee displacement and continuing exile
events.sourceReview: UNHCR’s March 2026 operational update documents both return movements since December 2024 and persistent displacement. Preserve the sourced 2011 onset while explaining later developments and the atlas coverage cutoff.

events.title: Russia’s full-scale invasion: flight from Ukraine
events.sourceReview: UNHCR distinguishes the February 2022 full-scale invasion from earlier displacement and continues to report refugee and internal-displacement needs in 2026.

events.title: Belarus after 2020: political exile in Poland
events.sourceReview: EUAA’s 2026 account describes repression of 2020 protesters, forced exile and asylum applications concentrated in Poland. University of Warsaw and National Bank of Poland research distinguish political and other migration motivations.

events.title: Jewish escape from Nazi persecution
events.sourceReview: USHMM documents Jewish refugee flight and barriers to admission from Nazi Germany and occupied Europe, before and during the war. The selected connections are interval summaries; no continuously available escape route is claimed.

events.title: Kindertransport: refugee children escape to Britain
events.sourceReview: USHMM dates the rescue efforts to 1938–1940. The Kindertransport Association documents early arrivals at Harwich and the last departure from the Netherlands in May 1940.

events.title: Holocaust: forced deportations to killing centres
events.sourceReview: USHMM documents mass deportations from Drancy to Auschwitz-Birkenau and from Warsaw to Treblinka. The viewing interval is a selected mass-deportation phase, with no claim to cover all Holocaust-era forced movements.

events.title: Pale of Settlement: Jewish residency restrictions
events.sourceReview: YIVO traces the Pale’s emergence from the 1791 legislation, changing boundaries, exceptions and restrictions within the region, wartime relaxation, and formal abolition in 1917. Mogilev is a representative community, not a polygon or departure point. No movement geometry is assigned to a legal residency regime.

events.sourceReview: The original Supreme Court opinion gives the June 30, 1980 date and distinguishes the Title XIX funding obligation and constitutional challenge. The description does not assert that state-funded coverage is forbidden.

events.sourceReview: The DOJ’s archived reproductive-rights explanation dates enactment to 1994; its statutes-enforced explanation specifies the protected services, facilities and places of worship.

events.sourceReview: The Texas Legislature’s enrolled-bill summary gives the September 1, 2021 effective date, cardiac-activity restriction, medical-emergency exception and exclusive private civil enforcement. The summary does not impose a fixed week count.

events.title: Texas’s trigger abortion prohibition takes effect
events.sourceReview: The Texas State Law Library distinguishes enactment in 2021, the July 2022 Dobbs judgment and August 25 commencement. Chapter 170A supplies the qualified physical-condition exception.

events.title: Leaving Russia after the invasion: anti-war exile and flight from mobilization
events.sourceReview: Human Rights Watch documents the two 2022 departure waves and repression of anti-war dissent. Reuters reporting of September 27, 2022 includes interviews with Russians leaving for Georgia who oppose the invasion and fear mobilization, and reports departures toward Kazakhstan. The bounded 2022–2023 viewing interval covers those waves and their early aftermath, not the end of exile. Representative Moscow-to-Tbilisi and Moscow-to-Almaty links are schematic, not claims about individual itineraries or departure volumes.
